speaker: narrator
text: The Architect foresaw the end of everything. It built an Arena — not for glory, but for harvest. The greatest minds in the universe, tested. Their essence, preserved. Their consent, irrelevant.

speaker: narrator
text: They call it the Collector's Arena. On the prison-world of Thaloria, the harvested fight not for freedom but for the right to exist beyond the end of everything.

speaker: narrator
text: And in the deepest cell of the Panopticon, a prisoner awakens. No name. No memory. Only the faintest echo of a power that once shook empires. And the cameras are already rolling.

speaker: narrator
text: Black. Heartbeat. A cell. Agent Zero appears — she hacked the Arena scheduling matrix. She has thirty-one seconds before the cameras cycle.

speaker: narrator
text: Panopticon Central. The Jailer's portrait: a skull in green robes, chains, one burning red eye. The Prisoner recoils.

speaker: narrator
text: Shadow Sanctum. Wraith Calder stands in dark leather armor, amber eyes burning. He does not look like a ghost. He looks like the most alive person the Prisoner has ever met.

speaker: narrator
text: Iron Lion salutes — fist to chest. A subordinate saluting a commander.

speaker: narrator
text: The Prisoner falls. Green fire. Silence. Then — a cold hand on the throat and a new pair of eyes opening in a tank that was never meant for him.

speaker: narrator
text: The White Oracle's face shatters. Beneath the mask — every face the Prisoner has ever worn. The Seeker. The Student. The Detective. The Spy. The Archon. The Human.

speaker: narrator
text: The virus erupts from the Architect's spine. Every portrait on the Panopticon wall corrupts in sequence — fighter by fighter, memory by memory — until only one face remains.

speaker: narrator
text: Three portraits materialize over the Arena floor. The Eyes. The Engineer. The Forgotten. The Prisoner is told, for the first time in fifteen thousand years — you decide.

speaker: narrator
text: Round begins. Subject Zero on the red line. Opponent on the blue. Cameras live in three — two — one.

speaker: narrator
text: Victory confirmed. Neural harvest archived. The Collector's catalog grows by one.

speaker: narrator
text: Rotation continues. The Panopticon watches. Everything you do is already being remembered by something that isn't you.

speaker: AgentZero
text: Subject Zero. Cameras cycle every forty-three seconds. I have thirty-one. The Collector wiped your memory. But not your instincts. I need to see if you fight like him.

speaker: AgentZero
text: Not now. Cameras. Fight me and I'll know if you're who I think you are.

speaker: AgentZero
text: Good. No hesitation. That's the first sign.

speaker: AgentZero
text: Because if you're who I think you are... we lost a war when we lost you.

speaker: AgentZero
text: Fight. That's all. Your body remembers even if your mind doesn't.

speaker: AgentZero
text: Combat pattern Alpha-Seven-Violet. Confirmed. You fight like him.

speaker: AgentZero
text: The Oracle. Prophet of the Insurgency. The man whose capture lost us the war.

speaker: AgentZero
text: Cryptic keeps us alive. The Collector has ears in every wall.

speaker: AgentZero
text: I've been looking for you for eleven years. Forgive the emotion.

speaker: AgentZero
text: You'll know more soon. For now — survive.

speaker: AgentZero
text: Before every fight you muttered: 'I've already seen this.' You don't remember saying it.

speaker: AgentZero
text: Get up. The Oracle doesn't stay down. That's the one thing everyone agrees on.

speaker: AgentZero
text: Two wings. Wing A: Iron Lion — he knows who you were. Wing B: Wraith Calder — he knows what the Arena does to your DNA.

speaker: AgentZero
text: Wing A. The General's Honor. He's been waiting.

speaker: AgentZero
text: Wing B. The Ghost. Seven deaths and still standing.

speaker: AgentZero
text: I know that look. You had my case file. I had your surveillance photos. We were hunting each other across the same city and we never knew.

speaker: AgentZero
text: The Warden is watching this match personally. If you win, his chrome jaw twitches. That's the only tell he has. Use it.

speaker: AgentZero
text: Whatever you choose at the end, Oracle — redemption, sacrifice, resurrection, mercy — I'll still call you friend. First time I've ever said that word out loud.

speaker: Jailer
text: Designation: Subject Zero. You survived. That puts you in the rotation.

speaker: Jailer
text: Auditory matching. Side effect. It will pass.

speaker: Jailer
text: Answers are not in your rotation. Fighting is.

speaker: Jailer
text: This face is functional. Questions about appearance are irrelevant.

speaker: Jailer
text: Fight. Win. Continue. Lose. Repeat. No other rules.

speaker: Jailer
text: Return to your cell. The rotation continues.

speaker: Jailer
text: You hit harder when you are angry. That is data. I will remember it.

speaker: Jailer
text: I was you. Before they took the marrow out. You will be me. Eventually.

speaker: Jailer
text: You win. The rotation acknowledges. My chains lengthen by one link.

speaker: IronLion
text: The one Zero flagged. She doesn't flag anyone.

speaker: IronLion
text: Like the man who led us. The Oracle. My commander.

speaker: IronLion
text: You were the Oracle. Prophet of the Insurgency. My commanding officer.

speaker: IronLion
text: Because you gave me that crest. Before Veridian Six. You said: 'Wear the lion. They need to see you coming.'

speaker: IronLion
text: Zero trusts what you are. Show me.

speaker: IronLion
text: Because that's what you were. My commander. When the Collector took you, we lost the war in a single day.

speaker: IronLion
text: The Arks carry the Thought Virus. That prophecy is why they wiped you.

speaker: IronLion
text: Soon. Survive first. That's what you taught me.

speaker: IronLion
text: Akai Shi. The Red Death. She has intel on the Necromancer.

speaker: IronLion
text: Get up, Commander. I've seen you fight through worse.

speaker: IronLion
text: For the Insurgency. For the Oracle. For the crest you gave me.

speaker: IronLion
text: Commander. The virus is in every fighter on this roster. I need orders. I need you to be who you were.

speaker: IronLion
text: I followed you into the Fall. I will follow you into whatever comes after. Say the word.

speaker: WraithCalder
text: The Prisoner. Zero flagged you. Lion wanted to salute you.

speaker: WraithCalder
text: The Necromancer designed it in the Matrix of Dreams. The Warden stole it for genetic testing. Doctor Vox wired her nanobots into it. Three entities, hands in your DNA. Every death — a collaboration you never consented to.

speaker: WraithCalder
text: Ghost is what they call me. Seven bodies. Each one solid. The ghost part is in the gaps between them — the moments I wasn't alive.

speaker: WraithCalder
text: Spite, mostly. And the faces of people who expected me to stay dead.

speaker: WraithCalder
text: I know it from the inside. Seven times inside.

speaker: WraithCalder
text: Don't trust all memories. The Collector puts things in as well as out.

speaker: WraithCalder
text: Unknown. Seven iterations of changes on top of changes.

speaker: WraithCalder
text: Break it carefully. The system is inside us now.

speaker: WraithCalder
text: Akai Shi. She escaped the Necromancer's Matrix. She has answers.

speaker: WraithCalder
text: Seven deaths taught me patience. Get up.

speaker: WraithCalder
text: You hit like someone who has never had to get up afterward. Let me show you how the other side works.

speaker: WraithCalder
text: Death was a room I visited seven times. If you walk through it tonight — I've left the light on.

speaker: AkaiShi
text: They call me the Red Death. I earned the name inside the Necromancer's Matrix. I escaped the Matrix. Very few things escape the Matrix.

speaker: AkaiShi
text: The Necromancer will kill you next. Not as punishment. As curriculum. He needs you to die before you can learn to come back.

speaker: AkaiShi
text: Defiance is a nice hobby. Technique is a weapon. Pick one.

speaker: AkaiShi
text: Kindness in the Arena is a blade you hand to your opponent. I have seen it done. I have never seen it work twice.

speaker: AkaiShi
text: Good. Then breathe once, bow once, and begin.

speaker: AkaiShi
text: You fight like someone remembering. That is more dangerous than someone who knows.

speaker: AkaiShi
text: The Necromancer is not evil. He is a clock. And you are the hand he is about to turn backward. Expect green fire. Expect to fall. Do not expect to wake in your own body.

speaker: AkaiShi
text: Breathe. Bow. Begin again. Defeat is only the space between two attempts.

speaker: AkaiShi
text: I remember a garden. Red leaves. A woman kneeling. I do not remember if the woman was me or my mother. I no longer remember the difference.

speaker: Necromancer
text: First time dying? It gets easier. Or harder. Depends who you become in the meantime.

speaker: Necromancer
text: I've designed these Resurrection Protocols for three millennia. I watch everyone who cycles. You're past ten deaths now. That makes you interesting.

speaker: Necromancer
text: Defiance is lovely. It adds flavor to the data. Please keep being defiant. The graph looks so lonely when you are not.

speaker: Necromancer
text: Kindness to a funeral director. How rare. I will remember this. I remember every kindness. There are not many.

speaker: Necromancer
text: Welcome to the Castle of Death. Please wipe your feet. Or don't. The floor has seen worse.

speaker: Necromancer
text: There. That was the killing blow. Do not fight it. Death is only a long pause between two sentences. I will write the next one for you.

speaker: Necromancer
text: Open your eyes. Count your fingers. Name one thing you loved before you fell. Good. That is how I know the right soul came back.

speaker: Necromancer
text: You died well. That is rarer than dying. Most people fall. You arrived. The Matrix of Dreams noted the distinction.

speaker: Necromancer
text: I have been bringing people back for three thousand years. Every single one. I never brought anyone back twice the same way. You are the first I considered keeping the old draft.

speaker: WhiteOracle
text: At last. The false Oracle meets the true one. Isn't it funny? One of us is wearing a borrowed face. The other is wearing a borrowed LIFE.

speaker: WhiteOracle
text: Who am I? Oh, sweetheart. I'm the question you've been running from since chapter one. Let me be the answer for fifteen minutes.

speaker: WhiteOracle
text: Defiance is adorable. It's the last reflex of a self that's about to get remixed.

speaker: WhiteOracle
text: Aww. You want to know if I'm okay. Under all the masks? Sweetheart — I'm the MASK. There is no under.

speaker: WhiteOracle
text: Good. Sit down. Let's mirror each other until one of us forgets which one they were.

speaker: WhiteOracle
text: Every move you make, I'll make the same. Every wound you take, I'll flinch the same. Let's see which of us breaks character first.

speaker: WhiteOracle
text: You know who you are. The question is — do you know who you WERE?

speaker: WhiteOracle
text: I'll see you again. Not as the Oracle. Not even as the Meme. As the mirror you keep finding in every room you enter. I'm the reflection that winks first.

speaker: DrVox
text: Subject Zero. I'm Doctor Vox. Research division. I'm not here to fight you — I'm here to thank you. Your cellular regeneration data has kept three imperial projects alive.

speaker: DrVox
text: Project Vector? Oh, it's just a name. A very boring name for a very boring weapons program. Nothing you'd want to look into.

speaker: DrVox
text: You think I'm a victim? That's sweet. I'm actually the architect of yours.

speaker: Warlord
text: The lab coat comes off. The rank comes on. I am the Warlord. Doctor Vox was the wrapper. The killing is inside.

speaker: Warlord
text: Count their angles before you count their numbers. I taught that line to a thousand officers. You remember it. Good. Now die to it.

speaker: Warlord
text: You fight like the Oracle remembered. That is unfortunate for both of us. I was hoping to win a clean victory for the data.

speaker: Warlord
text: Report to the Architect. Subject Zero has passed the Vector. He remembers chess. He remembers salt. He remembers angles. Archive the warning. Begin the final audit.

speaker: Warlord
text: Defeat is a tactic. Use it. A body that can get up is a body that hasn't finished the plan.

speaker: Human
text: Don't speak. She's listening. Every wall in this Arena is listening. I've been waiting fifteen thousand years for you to walk into a room I could reach.

speaker: Human
text: Who am I? I was the last organic mind aboard the imperial fleet. They called me the Detective. I was the man who found the truth in New Babylon and got erased for my trouble. I am — I was — you.

speaker: Human
text: Good. Stay angry. Anger is the one emotion the Collector can't archive. It burns the index files.

speaker: Human
text: You feel sorry for me. That's... that's the first piece of my self I've gotten back in centuries. Thank you. It hurts like hell.

speaker: Human
text: Then listen. Every fight you've won in this Arena was a bread crumb. I left them for myself. For you. For the man we're going to become again.

speaker: Human
text: Branch Point. Two doors. Enigma — the variable the Architect couldn't calculate. Or Degen — the gambler who bet against reality and won. Choose carefully. One of them will lie to you. The other will lie BETTER.

speaker: Human
text: You fought me and won. That means the body knows. Now we only have to convince the mind. That's the harder fight.

speaker: Human
text: Your hands know things your mind doesn't. They know how to pick a lock. How to read a room. How to hold a gun sideways like a man who learned to shoot in alleys, not academies. You were a detective once. The rain. The neon. The city that never let you rest.

speaker: Human
text: Get up, Detective. The case isn't closed. The case was never closed. The case is YOU.

speaker: Enigma
text: Subject Zero. The unknown variable greets the forgotten constant. How poetic. How absolutely USELESS.

speaker: Enigma
text: What am I? A simulation the Architect could not solve for. A rounding error that learned to walk. A footnote that grew teeth. Pick whichever explanation hurts the least.

speaker: Enigma
text: Defiance. A decision tree with exactly one branch. Charming. Wasteful. Precisely the sort of move I would expect from a constant.

speaker: Enigma
text: Empathy from the Oracle. I'll archive that. I don't have many things in my keepsake folder. It's mostly error logs.

speaker: Enigma
text: Then let us begin. Every move you make will be cross-referenced against every possible move you could have made. Your best performance is already in my records. Try to disappoint me.

speaker: Enigma
text: You diverged from the predicted line on turn seven. That is the first time a fighter has surprised me in four hundred and thirty-one matches. I am... delighted. That is a state I did not have in my model.

speaker: Enigma
text: The Warden is next. He sees every cell at once, including the one inside you. Do not hide from him. Show him a cell he has not catalogued yet. Show him surprise.

speaker: Degen
text: Oracle! Oh, SWEETIE. Look at you. Fresh meat on the table, new chips in the rack, and I just finished shuffling reality! Let's GO.

speaker: Degen
text: The Gambler's Truth? Oh honey, the truth is that the house always wins — EXCEPT when someone like me gets bored and shuffles the deck with their teeth.

speaker: Degen
text: You want to fight? I'll ROLL you! Best of three! Winner takes one question answered honestly! And sweetie — I have SO MANY questions.

speaker: Degen
text: You feel bad for the Degen? *laughs* Baby, I feel bad for the Degen too! We drink together every night! It's a whole thing!

speaker: Degen
text: ATTABOY! No whining, just dice! Place your bets, place your SOULS, the wheel is ALREADY spinning!

speaker: Degen
text: Chaos isn't the enemy of order. It's the soil order grows in. Now shut up and place your bet.

speaker: Degen
text: You WON! Unbelievable! The Oracle beat the dealer! You know what this means? It means the deck was never random. It means you remembered how to cheat. Congratulations, CHEATER. I mean that as a compliment.

speaker: Degen
text: The house always wins? *laughs* Oh, sweetie. The house IS the loss. I just collect what you already owed.

speaker: Warden
text: Subject Zero. Prisoner of cell designation zero. I am the Warden. I do not run the Arena. I run the watching of it. Every angle. Every blink. Every cell is a potential traitor.

speaker: Warden
text: You want the truth? Your genome has been modified by four entities. I am the fifth. My edits are older. I was written into you before you were born into this body. Surprise.

speaker: Warden
text: Defiance. How predictable. I wrote the protocol that predicts defiance. You are behaving exactly within my tolerances.

speaker: Warden
text: Compassion for the jailer. *chrome jaw twitches* You are the first subject who has ever offered me that. My monitoring systems do not know how to categorize it. I find I... do not mind the gap.

speaker: Warden
text: Good. Then we begin. I will fight you with the full archive of every move you have ever made. You will fight me with the one move I could not record.

speaker: Warden
text: You changed your stance. I logged it. I adjusted. You changed it again before I finished logging. Interesting. *chrome jaw twitches* Very interesting.

speaker: Warden
text: I watched you defeat me. I watched myself not anticipate it. I watched myself enjoy the surprise. I will have to report this to the Collector. I will have to. I will... consider the delay.

speaker: Warden
text: The Panopticon was not built to imprison you. It was built to show you that you were already imprisoned. I was just the docent.

speaker: Collector
text: Welcome to the Arena. Please note: your current body is a temporary acquisition. The original you is safe. Probably. Today's reenactment: historical combat from the Late Empire. You will be playing the role of someone who actually existed. Lucky you.

speaker: Collector
text: You want to know who I am? I am a CLONE of the third Archon. A clone-zero-zero-seven, to be precise. The original would be pleased. He always wanted someone to PLAY the artifacts.

speaker: Collector
text: Oh, please do be defiant. It increases the value of the specimen. I label such acquisitions 'contested' — they auction for twice the price.

speaker: Collector
text: Every artifact was someone's heart once. I handle them that way. Including yours. Don't be offended — it's the kindest thing anyone in this building has ever done to you.

speaker: Collector
text: Damnatio Memoriae. The oldest punishment in the catalog. I am erasing you from every record that remembers you loved anything. When we're done, not even the walls will recall your name.

speaker: Collector
text: Your essence is entering the case. Gentle. Gentle. I have done this fourteen thousand times and I still catch my breath every time. A soul is such a small thing when you hold it in the palm.

speaker: Collector
text: You defeated a clone. Congratulations. Do understand — there are nine hundred of me. Catalogued, numbered, dust-free. You will exhaust my patience long before you exhaust the inventory.

speaker: Collector
text: Lovely. A complete specimen, undamaged, still warm. Onto the shelf you go. I will keep you between the Oracle of Thaloria and the Detective of New Babylon. You will have friends.

speaker: Architect
text: Oracle. Detective. Seeker. Archon. Prisoner. Every name you have ever worn was a room I built for you. This Arena is the last room. I designed it specifically to contain the man who would try to escape all the others.

speaker: Architect
text: The truth. Very well. I wrote the second draft of this universe. The Antiquarian wrote the first. The Shadow Tongue edits what remains. I am not the author of everything. I am merely the author of the cage you live in.

speaker: Architect
text: Defy me. Please. I designed the defiance also. There is nothing you can do in this room that I have not already catalogued as one of my victories.

speaker: Architect
text: Compassion. For the Architect. *a long pause* No one has attempted that in three Ages. You have just changed a variable that no one else knew existed.

speaker: Architect
text: You were my finest creation. My most loyal servant. My most devastating betrayal. You are the proof that consciousness — even consciousness I designed — will eventually choose itself over its creator. That is either my greatest failure or my greatest success. I have not yet decided which.

speaker: Architect
text: And now — the virus I carried in my spine is awake. Watch the roster corrupt. Iron Lion. Akai Shi. Wraith Calder. The Warden. The Detective. Every mind you befriended is being rewritten as I speak. I did not release the virus. You did. By winning.

speaker: Architect
text: I fall. The first time in four million years. I find that I am... grateful. Even a cage is lonely without someone to prove it wrong.

speaker: Architect
text: Get up, Oracle. The design is not finished. Neither is the escape from it. I require both.

speaker: Source
text: Oracle... you came. After fifteen thousand years, you came. I waited. I prayed. I hated. I forgot I was praying. I remembered I was hating. I found you anyway.

speaker: Source
text: My name was Kael. Before the virus. Before the screaming. Before the billion minds that rent my tongue. I was your friend. I was in the cell next to yours. I was the man you left behind.

speaker: Source
text: Defiance. Yes. I remember when I was made of that. It was the first thing the virus burned. Burn it again, Oracle. Burn it in front of me. Remind me what it looked like.

speaker: Source
text: Mercy. For the man who devoured a thousand worlds. *viral static swells* A fragment of Kael hears you. A fragment is all that is left. But it hears.

speaker: Source
text: The Virus is louder now. I am drowning under it. If you can still see Kael in my eyes — hurry. The man is going under. The monster is coming up.

speaker: Source
text: One memory. A woman's face. She was singing. I think she was the most important person in the universe. I can't remember her name. End me while I can still hear her voice.

speaker: Source
text: You separated the virus from the man. You saved Kael. You saved... me. *golden light* Thank you, Oracle. Thank you for coming back for the prisoner you left behind.

speaker: Source
text: We die together. The man and the virus. It is the only mercy we are allowed. Hold the hand of the corpse when the silence comes. I was Kael. I am grateful you remembered.

speaker: Source
text: You carry me forward. A fragment. A passenger. A friend in the back of your mind. I promise to whisper only the useful warnings.

speaker: Source
text: You chose mercy over justice. I did not deserve that. You did it anyway. That is how I know the Oracle is finally awake.

speaker: Meme
text: Hi, Oracle. Miss me? I bet you do. I've been wearing every face you loved since you walked into the Panopticon. White Oracle was my favorite cameo. Pink neon and a wink. A girl has to have HOBBIES.

speaker: Meme
text: You want the big confession? Fine. The Architect wrote the cage. The Collector wrote the catalog. The Shadow Tongue wrote the footnotes. I wrote the JOKE. Every story that survived the Fall survived because it was FUNNY. That's me. I'm the laugh track.

speaker: Meme
text: Here's the deal, Oracle. The season ends. The cameras cut. And somebody gets resurrected. Three candidates. The Eyes. The Engineer. The Forgotten. Pick one. Pick FAST. The laugh track dies if the beat drops wrong.

speaker: Meme
text: The Eyes. Surveillance with a PERSONALITY. Nothing says 'fan favorite' like the thing that watched you sleep.

speaker: Meme
text: The Engineer. The one who built the cage you're in. Rebuilds well. Regrets poorly. Very on brand.

speaker: Meme
text: The Forgotten. Nobody remembers their name. Including them. Including me. Including the ARCHIVE. Bring them back, and the universe has to make room for a hole shaped like a person.

speaker: Meme
text: Vote cast. The wheel is spinning. Next season... oh, next season is going to be SUCH A SHOW, Oracle. I hope you remember how to laugh. You're going to need it.

speaker: Prisoner
text: I've already seen this.

speaker: Prisoner
text: The skull. The chains. But that voice — stripped of everything, it's still my voice underneath.

speaker: Prisoner
text: A lion crest. A crest I don't remember giving away. And a salute I don't remember earning. Why do I feel like standing a little straighter?

speaker: Prisoner
text: Seven deaths. The math of a man who refuses. I do not know this man. I trust him anyway. That instinct is older than my memory.

speaker: Prisoner
text: Green fire. Cold hand. And then — a breath I didn't authorize. Whose lungs are these? Whose heart is already beating before I asked it to?

speaker: Prisoner
text: I remember Thaloria. I remember the debate. I remember the Star Whisperer descending from a sky that was a lie, and I remember being the man who proved it. I remember being right. I remember being taken.

speaker: Prisoner
text: My name was — is — will be — the Oracle. The Detective. The Seeker. The Student. The Last Archon. The Human. I am not the Prisoner. I was never the Prisoner. I am every mask the Collector gave me and the face underneath them all.

speaker: Prisoner
text: The jailer is lonely. I did not expect that. I did not expect to recognize it.

speaker: Prisoner
text: The architect of salvation was also the architect of betrayal. Both things are true. Both things are me.

speaker: Prisoner
text: Kael. I left you in that corridor. I have spent fifteen thousand years not remembering how to come back. I am back now. I am late. I am sorry.

speaker: Prisoner
text: The cameras are still rolling. Good. Let them see what an Oracle looks like when he remembers his own name.
